intro.title:
Two countries.
One water problem.
intro.lede: The Australia India Water Centre is a partnership of {{partnerInstitutions}} institutions and {{researchers}} researchers, working together on research, education, training and outreach for sustainable water futures.

blocks.title: What we do
blocks.lede: AIWC’s key activities are structured into four distinct areas. Each has two or more programme leaders, who meet six times a year to plan, design and oversee activities across partners and stakeholders.

items.title: Research
items.text: Joint projects across Australian and Indian institutions, several funded under India’s SPARC scheme.

items.title: Education
items.text: A transdisciplinary Master’s program in Sustainable Water Management.

items.title: Training & capacity building
items.text: Five programmes, from village-level groundwater monitoring to dam safety training.

items.title: Outreach
items.text: Workshops, webinars and technical exchange between researchers, policy-makers and practitioners.

blocks.lede: Symposia, podcasts and the WATER TALKS webinar series — open to researchers, policy-makers, practitioners and students across Australia, India and the Asia Pacific.

left.lead: The Centre acts as a catalyst for Australian and Indian partners to break down silos, think differently, and facilitate sustainable water futures through bilateral partnerships and transdisciplinary approaches.
paragraphs: Water is a global resource that matters to everyone and everything we do. More than ever, we need to understand and work together on water issues and challenges, now and in the future — and those issues need to be addressed with collective concerns, experiences, learnings and efforts.
Leading Australian and Indian institutions, government agencies and water businesses came together to form the Centre in 2020, led by Western Sydney University in Australia and IIT Guwahati in India.

photo.alt: Partners in a round-table discussion at AIWC@5

blocks.title: Five years, and the next five.

items.title: 2020 — The Centre launches
items.text: AIWC is launched on 6 November 2020 — the first collaborative centre of its kind — led by Western Sydney University in Australia and IIT Guwahati in India, with 24 partners across the two countries.

items.title: 2021 — WaterWise begins
items.text: On World Environment Day, core members initiate WaterWise: a virtual water dialogue where participants are contributors rather than passive receivers of knowledge.

items.title: 2022 — Technical exchange with government
items.text: Four workshops with the Australia India Institute under the Joint Working Group convened by DAWE and the Ministry of Jal Shakti — groundwater, soil and water, wastewater reuse, and water informatics.

items.title: 2024–25 — Training at scale
items.text: Forty Young Water Professionals trained from India’s central and state water departments; a second cohort of fifteen Indian Dam Safety Officers completes a two-week programme across NSW.

items.title: 2025 — AIWC@5 and the 2030 agenda
items.text: Around 80 delegates gather at the Whitlam Institute for the Partners Forum and International Symposium; the AIWC Five-Year Report launches and five breakout sessions set the 2030 agenda.

blocks.title: Our partners
blocks.lede: Universities, national institutes, government departments and water businesses in Australia and India.

blocks.heading: AIWC is looking for partners for the 2030 agenda.
blocks.body: Climate-resilient agriculture, groundwater security, PFAS and water quality, digital water tools, joint degree programmes and micro-credentials — the priorities set by partners at AIWC@5. If your institution works in any of them, we would like to hear from you.
